The product is browser-based: AI and algorithmic models analyse markets, surface signals and suggest entries, with automatic or manual execution. Registration is free, the demo runs alongside, and the minimum deposit sits at US$250.
The checks below follow the platform published pages in order - what it claims, what the fine print says, and where the two diverge. The verdict is a summary of those checks, nothing more.
whatItClaims: A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
whatWeChecked: The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.
The ownership trail: who operates the platform and where.
The support channels: live chat, email or phone availability.
The fine print: clauses that qualify the headline promises.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Fill in the registration form and activate the account via the confirmation email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Add US$250 to the account through the payment options shown at checkout.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set the risk parameters, decide between automatic and manual, and practise on the demo account.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Unfilled template placeholders.
No verified track record.
One figure doing two different jobs.
Return claims without verification.
redFlags: Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
The scorecard settles at 4.8. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.
